source: lab (captured; background outside ball/table blurred, 'Modified with Segment Anything 2 Demo' watermark bottom-right)
time_convention: t = frame / 24; frame = round(t*24); frame 0 at t=0

camera.motion: static (tripod-mounted; table edges and background fixed across all frames)
camera.intrinsics_from_benchmark: Orbbec Femto Mega RGB, HFOV 80 deg: f = 0.5959*1280 = 763 px, principal point ~ (640, 360)
camera.perspective: camera looks slightly down at a tabletop; tabletop front edge (~y 484-497) much wider in px than back edge (~y 420-430) => strong perspective, table close to camera. Image y of a point on the tabletop increases as it comes toward the camera.

objects.name: ball
objects.description: small white ping-pong-type ball (only white round object), held in the person's right-hand fingertips above the table, then dropped and bounces on the tabletop
objects.apparent_size_note: diameter (bbox_w, horizontal, unaffected by vertical blur) grows ~17 -> ~25 px: ball moves toward the camera during the bounces; depth ~ f*D/width_px

objects.name: table
objects.description: wooden (light-brown) tabletop on a single dark central post, centre of image
objects.post: dark vertical pole below the top, x ~ 710-750, from y ~515 to image bottom
objects.note: right back corner partially hidden by the person's hand/arm; corners approximate +-5 px

objects.name: person
objects.description: person with long dark hair (face blurred/masked) standing behind the table, leaning forward; right hand holds and drops the ball; left hand rests near table right edge
objects.moves: slightly (arm/hand raise the ball frames 12-21, then hand moves away/down); body roughly static
objects.note: heavily blurred by the background replacement; not tracked

objects.name: tripod_light_stand
objects.description: background tripod stand with a light on top (blurred), behind table, top at ~ (688, 70)

objects.name: wall_panels / floor
objects.description: grey wall panels and grey/red carpet floor, blurred

events.event: hand raises ball (slow upward motion ~2-3 px/frame)
release (top of lift, ball starts falling from rest)
